doll.excerpt: Listen, Vasilissa, dear; remember and obey these last words of mine. I am going to die. And now, together with my parental blessing, I bequeath to you this doll. Keep it always by you, and never show it to anybody; and whenever any misfortune comes upon you, give the doll food, and ask its advice.

task.excerpt: The doll had cleared the wheat to the very last grain. "Ah, my preserver!" cried Vasilissa, "you've saved me from danger!" "All you've got to do now is to cook the dinner," answered the doll, slipping into Vasilissa's pocket. "Cook away, in God's name, and then take some rest for your health's sake!" Towards evening Vasilissa got the table ready, and awaited the Baba Yaga. It began to grow dusky; the black rider appeared for a moment at the gate, and all grew dark. Only the eyes of the skulls sent forth their light. The trees began to crack, the leaves began to rustle, up drove the Baba Yaga. Vasilissa went out to meet her. "Is everything done?" asks the Yaga. "Please to look for yourself, granny!" says Vasilissa.
task.note: Verbatim Ralston text; distinguish his collection, translation, or folkloristic summary from the tale traditions he discusses.

narrativeBlocks.title: A gift with instructions
narrativeBlocks.body: Before she dies, Vasilissa's mother gives her a doll and tells her to feed it and ask for counsel when trouble comes.

narrativeBlocks.title: The mother's instructions
narrativeBlocks.body: Source quotation (Ralston's English text; whitespace normalized): “Listen, Vasilissa, dear; remember and obey these last words of mine. I am going to die. And now, together with my parental blessing, I bequeath to you this doll. Keep it always by you, and never show it to anybody; and whenever any misfortune comes upon you, give the doll food, and ask its advice.”

narrativeBlocks.title: The work is done
narrativeBlocks.body: At Baba Yaga's house, Vasilissa fears she will fail. The doll clears the wheat while she rests, allowing her to face the morning inspection.

narrativeBlocks.title: Stay with this collected tale
narrativeBlocks.body: Ralston presents this as Vasilissa the Fair, a Russian folktale. Do not turn one tale's doll into evidence of a universal Slavic household ritual.

narrativeBlocks.title: Help is relational
narrativeBlocks.body: The doll's help follows Vasilissa's care and her mother's instruction; the tale connects survival with attention and trust.
